premise: Settlers built a town inside the bones of a fallen god. The marrow still hums.
tone: Dark with humor: a bleak world full of funny, petty, very human people.
magic: Like Eragon's: infinitely flexible but dangerous. Spoken in the dead god's own tongue, paid for out of the caster's body. Learn it from a teacher, or gamble your life learning alone.
genre_bend: High fantasy under the rib bones: old lineages (the Bearer families who hauled the god's corpse) hold hereditary rights, a fractured pantheon left songs and grudges, and the rising dark is the goddess who killed him coming back to finish the job. Pastoral town life, gossip and tithe disputes, played straight against a cosmic murder that is not quite over.
art_style: In the style of a classic 1980s oil-painted fantasy paperback cover, thick visible brushstrokes and warm hand-painted figures, but lit from below by the sickly amber-and-ivory glow of living god-marrow, with deep violet shadows pooling between colossal curved rib bones that frame every scene like cathedral arches.
chronicler_persona: Illuminator-in-residence to the Chapel of the Long Wake, paid by the canvas and paid badly. Earnest, devout, flatters whoever commissioned the piece, adds a halo to anyone who tips, and signs every work with a small apologetic note about the varnish.
